claims.text: The proposed material for studying lattice heat conductivity is high-purity SiO2.
Introducing controlled SRO precipitates into high-purity SiO2 will increase phonon scattering rates.
Introducing controlled SRO precipitates into high-purity SiO2 will reduce its lattice thermal conductivity relative to precipitate-free SiO2.
The initial material is 99.999% pure SiO2.
High-purity SiO2 has negligible electronic conduction.
Annealing SiO2 at 1100°C for 2 hours will induce SRO precipitates.
The induced SRO precipitates will have diameters of 5–10 nm.
The induced SRO precipitates will have a density of approximately 10^20 cm^-3.
At room temperature, heat transport in the proposed SiO2 material is dominated by lattice phonons and electronic thermal contributions are negligible.
Nanoscale SRO precipitates act as phonon-scattering centers.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces phonon mean free paths and scattering times.
Reduced phonon mean free paths and scattering times lower lattice thermal conductivity.
SiO2 containing induced SRO precipitates will show a measurable reduction in lattice thermal conductivity relative to pristine high-purity SiO2.
Precipitate-free high-purity SiO2 has higher lattice thermal conductivity because its phonon scattering times are longer.
The proposed effect is expected to apply to insulating materials with negligible electronic thermal transport.
The magnitude of the effect may vary substantially with precipitate morphology or density.
